title: staged-safety-umbrella and customer escalation wiring for noisy model rollouts
creator: Maya Patel
description: Objective: Create a lightweight, deterministic 'safety umbrella' that can be activated during noisy model rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments to stabilize customer-facing traffic while we remediate regressions. The wiring must cover automated tenant pinning, rapid model variant fallback, KV-cache reconciliation guidance, and an operator communication plan to eliminate delay between detection and customer-facing mitigation.
acceptance_criteria: Activate safety umbrella halts risky canary traffic within 60s for hosted and dedicated routes
Tenant-level pinning can be scheduled and reversed via API and Console for Dedicated/Private without full deployment rollback
Model-variant fallback executes a compatibility check and routes <=10% traffic to fallback within 30s without overwriting KV cache
Operator playbook in Console exists with one-click links to dashboards, runbooks, and canned customer messaging
Post-activation reconciliation tasks documented and automated where safe (KV rehydrate, cache invalidation, traffic re-slice)
resolution_plan: Phase 1: Implement API + Console 'safety umbrella' toggle that performs: 1) immediate traffic hold for new canaries, 2) tenant pin to last-known-good model, 3) route-level throttles
Phase 2: Add automated model-variant compatibility check (shape/kv-keyspace/quantization fingerprint) and fallback wiring. If mismatch, fallback aborts and notifies.
Phase 3: Provide KV cache reconciliation checklist and a small automation (safe rehydrate job) for cases where rollout caused cache divergence
Phase 4: Document operator runbook, on-call handoff template, and templated customer comms for SRE/Support teams
Phase 5: Run two dry-runs with synthetic slices and one shadow-run against a low-traffic customer to validate end-to-end behaviour
comments: 2026-02-20 - Maya Patel (creator): Drafted scope and acceptance criteria after incident on 2026-02-18 where a canary introduced hallucination spike for 4 enterprise tenants. Key ask from support: faster tenant-level mitigation without full rollback.

2026-02-22 - Diego Alvarez (assignee): Spike completed to validate tenant pin API. Results: pin applied server-side in under 2s for hosted; Dedicated required a control-plane RPC update (estimated 30s). Will implement async confirmation to UI.

2026-02-26 - Tech review (SRE/Serving): We debated an immediate global circuit-breaker vs tenant-scoped umbrella. Decision: tenant-scoped preferred to avoid collateral damage; global circuit-breaker kept as last-resort P0 action.

2026-03-01 - Design feedback (Alejandra Cruz): Console mockups added — one-click 'safety umbrella' with prefilled customer messaging. Requested an extra confirmation step for private on-prem customers.
2026-03-03 - PR opened: runtime #2874 implements safety umbrella API endpoints and a light state machine. Linking QA plan. @eng-qa requested additional e2e for KV cache staleness.

2026-03-05 - Incident reenactment: Dry-run on staging with synthetic tenant slice. Observed fallout: fallback route applied but KV cache rehydration lagged causing transient latency. Mitigation: enqueue safe rehydrate job with backoff and progress events to Console.
2026-03-08 - Product review (Nora Singh): Approved scope for Phase 1 & 2; requested measurable SLOs (time to mitigation, percent traffic stabilized). Added to rollout-resilience project.
2026-03-10 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented UI confirmation for private deployments and added webhook to notify support workspace. Preparing changelog and runbook updates for release runtime-2.4.1
followups: Post-release: monitor rollback telemetry for 2 weeks and run tenant reconciliation job nightly for first 48h
Create a small CLI utility for SRE to perform tenant pinning in air-gapped private deployments
Add automated customer-facing metrics snapshot to support ticket when umbrella activates
